name: ThinQuant: Scalable Rotation Learning for Weight and Activation Quantization of LLMs
problem: Gradient-based rotation learning (SpinQuant) is too expensive at frontier scale, and even gradient-free rotation learning (DartQuant) needs too much calibration data and wall-clock.
mechanism: Two efficiency ideas for rotation learning. (1) Data selection using the geometric structure of the CONVEX HULL of the activations, which picks a calibration set orders of magnitude smaller than prior rotation methods. (2) Because that reduced set spans an r-dimensional subspace with r < d, optimizing the full d x d rotation reduces exactly to optimizing a d x r matrix on the Stiefel manifold, solved with an efficient ADMM algorithm using thin matrix updates at every step. Same mechanism class as QuaRot/SpinQuant, made scalable.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): with a calibration set orders of magnitude smaller than state-of-the-art rotation methods, matching their low-bit quantization performance. CONCRETE: Llama-3-70B at W4A4KV4 completes rotation calibration in UNDER 12 MINUTES with WikiText-2 perplexity 5.63, versus 7.55 for DartQuant which requires 111 minutes. Llama-3.1-405B at W4A4: calibration in just over 2 HOURS on a SINGLE H200, WikiText-2 perplexity 2.97 versus 3.48 for GPTAQ+QuaRot. COMPRESSION RATIO: 4-bit weights, activations and KV cache. QUALITY COST: 5.63 and 2.97 perplexity against full-precision baselines that the abstract does not print - so these are relative comparisons, not quality costs.
